title: Impact of Catalytic Converter Mandate on NOx Emissions

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)

Why:  
• The policy is introduced in only a subset of regions (treated = 1), creating treated and control groups.  
• We observe each region before (post = 0) and after (post = 1) the mandate.  
• The interaction treat_x_post isolates the policy’s causal effect.

Key assumption – Parallel Trends:  
In the absence of the mandate, treated and control regions would have experienced the same average change in log NOx emissions over time. We will partially validate this with a pre-trend (placebo) test.

## 2. R Code
```r
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#  Catalytic Converter Mandate – DID Estimation
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Required packages
required_pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest", "ggplot2")
for(p in required_pkgs) if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly=TRUE)) install.packages(p)
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Read data ------------------------------------------------
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s47_data.csv"
dt <- fread(data_path)

# 2. Basic two‐way fixed-effects DID --------------------------
#   y_it = α_i + δ_t + β*Treat×Post_it + ε_it
did_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n===== Baseline DID estimate =====\n")
etable(did_twfe, se = "cluster")

# Extract and print the coefficient of interest
beta <- coef(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
se_beta <- se(did_twfe)["treat_x_post"]
cat(sprintf("\nEstimated policy effect (β̂): %.4f  (SE = %.4f)\n", beta, se_beta))

# 3. Robustness check 1: Allow unit-specific trends -----------
dt[, period_c := period - min(period)]  # centred time
did_trend <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + i(unit_id, period_c) | unit_id + period,
                   data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n===== DID with unit-specific linear trends =====\n")
etable(did_trend, se = "cluster")

# 4. Robustness check 2: Pre-trend (placebo) test -------------
# Create a fake "placebo" interaction for one period before the mandate
# Assume the mandate starts at the first post==1; placebo at post_t1 where period == (start-1)
start_period <- dt[post == 1, min(period)]
dt[, placebo := as.integer(treated == 1 & period == (start_period - 1))]

placebo_model <- feols(y ~ placebo | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)
cat("\n===== Placebo (pre-trend) test =====\n")
etable(placebo_model, se = "cluster")

# 5. Visualization: Event-study style graph -------------------
# Generate leads/lags of treatment
dt[, rel_time := period - start_period]               # 0 = first treated period
es_model <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                  data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

png("event_study_plot.png", 800, 500)
iplot(es_model, xlab = "Periods relative to mandate", ylab = "Effect on log NOx",
      main = "Event-study plot: Catalytic Converter Mandate")
dev.off()
cat("\nEvent-study plot saved as 'event_study_plot.png'\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative. The catalytic converter mandate should reduce NOx emissions, so the coefficient β̂ on treat_x_post is expected to be < 0.

Magnitude: Because the outcome is in logs, a coefficient around −0.15 to −0.30 would imply a 14–26 % reduction in NOx emissions in treated regions relative to controls after the mandate. 

Rationale: Prior environmental regulations of similar scope typically cut vehicular NOx by roughly 20 %. A log-point change of −0.2 is therefore plausible.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in log NOx emissions between treated and untreated regions over time.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The catalytic converter mandate significantly reduces log NOx emissions.
